bindings.label: Severe chest pain radiating to back with dyspnea and sweating occurred about 30 minutes post-procedure

79-year-old female patient initially presented with severe chest pain lasting 4 hours; medical history includes moderately managed hypertension, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation treated with Betaloc for 6 months, moderate pulmonary hypertension (pulmonary artery systolic pressure ~55 mmHg), and no diabetes or hyperlipidemia
Initial vital signs during procedure showed low blood pressure 60/40 mmHg, which improved to 90/50 mmHg with heart rate 96 beats/min after intervention
Post-procedure vital signs showed blood pressure 100-111/54-70 mmHg, SpO2 84%, and heart rate 110-142 beats/min
Imaging reveals pericardial effusion with contrast leakage from myocardium to pericardial cavity
Imaging shows no intimal flap or false lumen in the aorta
Coronary angiography shows only tiny distal LCx occlusion, insufficient to explain hemodynamic collapse
